title: read_vasp compatible with reading lattice velocities, and atomic velocity reading also fixed
body:
Closes #1714

Also, the reading of atomic velocities was also not working (sees the starting empty line and then quits), so I have also fixed this.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
This line would be empty for a normal POSCAR, and in such a case, accessing `[0]` causes an error.
To avoid this, we should first check if this is a non-empty line, maybe as
```python
    if velocity_init_line.strip() and velocity_init_line[0].lower() == 'l':
```
(The `if velocity_init_line.strip()` part checks if this is a non-empty line.)
comments.label_reasoning: Accessing [0] on an empty string for normal POSCAR files causes an IndexError; missing edge case check for empty line.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Identifies a bug (IndexError on empty line) and provides a specific code fix.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body: Please have "two" blank lines before this line, to follow [PEP8](https://peps.python.org/pep-0008/#blank-lines).
comments.label_reasoning: PEP8 requires two blank lines before top-level definitions; this is a blank line/whitespace standards violation.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests a specific formatting change (two blank lines) to comply with PEP8.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Assigning unused variables is better to be avoided. I would suggest:
```python
...
    fd.readline()  # initialization state
    for _ in range(3):  # lattice velocities
        fd.readline()
    for _ in range(3):  # lattice vectors
        fd.readline()
    fd.readline()  # get rid of 1 empry line below


def read_velocities_if_present(fd, natoms) -> np.ndarray | None:
...
```
comments.label_reasoning: Variables are assigned but never used; the reviewer suggests discarding return values with fd.readline() directly.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Suggests removing unused variable assignments and provides a concrete code refactor.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
To follow PEP8 and make the line less than 80 characters, let's rephrase this comment.
Since the `read the 1st line` is obvious, we can omit it e.g., as:
```
    # Check if it is the velocities block or the MD extra block
```
comments.label_reasoning: Comment exceeds 80 characters and violates PEP8 line length; reviewer requests rephrasing to comply with style guidelines.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests a comment be rephrased for PEP8 compliance and line length, with a specific suggested replacement.

comments.author: yuzie007
comments.body:
Thank you @sunghjung3 for the MR!

The change looks mostly reasonable.
There is one bug related to `velocity_init_line` for normal POSCAR files; please see my comment above and kindly fix it.
You can then check if the `pytest ase/test/fio/vasp` command passes (if you install `pytest`).

You can also add a change-log file using `scriv`. Please follow [here](https://wiki.fysik.dtu.dk/ase/development/writing_changelog.html), then you can modify the created file e.g. as
```rst
I/O
---

- Fix :class:`~ase.io.vasp.read_vasp` for a POSCAR with lattice velocities
  (:mr:`3762`)
```

If possible, it would be nice if you turn on CI pipelines on your forked repo; maybe you can follow https://gitlab.com/sunghjung3/ase/-/jobs/10805296500.
Then reviewers can easily check if the present MR does not break the existing codes.
comments.label_reasoning: General review comment summarizing the bug with velocity_init_line for normal POSCAR files, pointing back to the logic error identified in comment 0.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: Requests a bug fix, suggests adding a changelog file, and recommends enabling CI pipelines — multiple concrete action items.
